source_title: Hill & Smith Holdings PLC Annual Report for the year ended 31 December 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 115 and 167 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 4 March 2020; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 9%, underlying operating profit 8% and profit before tax 4%, but Group margin eased 20 basis points, cash conversion fell to 67%, ROIC declined and net debt increased. A small Scandinavian roads operation was loss-making amid difficult conditions and was already being restructured, while the core UK and US businesses remained profitable and growing.
already_announced_exclusion: The Scandinavian management changes, depot closures, Norway exit and related restructuring actions disclosed or undertaken before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Specific operating pressure, weaker cash conversion and higher debt are material, but the affected operation was small and already under action while Group revenue, profit and the dividend continued to grow.

source_title: Hill & Smith Holdings PLC Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 127 and 176 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 9 March 2022; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 7%, underlying operating profit 23%, margin improved from 10.6% to 12.2%, ROIC rose and covenant leverage fell to 1.0x with substantial financing headroom. Supply-chain, inflation and labour pressure affected selected businesses, with impairments and closures already recognised, but all three divisions delivered organic revenue and profit growth.
already_announced_exclusion: The Technocover disposal, Variable Message Signs closure, Swedish rental disposal process and associated impairment and reorganisation charges disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Selected businesses faced specific pressure, but broad revenue, profit and margin growth, lower leverage, high cash generation and ample headroom provide strong contrary evidence.
